scope_note: Prototype knowledge base for a binary leaf-health verdict. The infected entry lists probable causes to scout for; it does not assert a single diagnosis, because the vision model is a binary healthy/infected detector trained on procedurally generated imagery.

healthy.what_is_happening_en: The leaf shows an even green colour with no necrotic spots, no yellowing between the veins and no feeding damage. No treatment is needed today.
symptoms: even green colour across the leaf blade
no holes, trails or chewed edges

organic_treatment.interval: once every 15 days as a preventive spray
organic_treatment.note: spray in the evening so the leaf does not scorch

prevention: scout 10 plants in each corner of the field once a week
water at the base with drip or a hose instead of overhead spraying
remove and burn crop residue after harvest
keep 45 to 60 cm between plants so air moves freely
rotate to a non-host crop for two to three seasons

urgency.trace: No action needed. Keep scouting once a week.
urgency.mild: No action needed. Keep scouting once a week.
urgency.moderate: No action needed. Keep scouting once a week.
urgency.severe: No action needed. Keep scouting once a week.

scouting: check the lower older leaves first, because most leaf diseases start there
turn leaves over and look at the underside for insects

region_notes.default: Scout more often during humid weather and after continuous rain.
region_notes.tamil_nadu: During the north-east monsoon from October to December, scout twice a week because long leaf wetness favours leaf disease.
region_notes.punjab: Scout closely during February and March as temperature and humidity rise.
region_notes.maharashtra: Scout twice a week in the kharif season when humidity stays high.

sources: ICAR Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, integrated disease management advisories
Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Crop Protection Guide

infected.headline_en: This leaf shows disease or pest damage
infected.what_is_happening_en: The leaf shows dead or discoloured tissue. Part of the leaf can no longer feed the plant. Act early, because leaf damage spreads to healthy leaves in warm and humid weather.
symptoms: brown or black dead patches on the leaf blade
yellowing of tissue around the damaged area
grey or water-soaked patches, often starting at the leaf margin
small dark spots spread across the blade
holes, winding trails or chewed edges where an insect has fed
conditions: warm weather between 20 and 30 degrees Celsius
high humidity or leaves that stay wet for more than six hours
dense planting with poor air movement
overhead irrigation that splashes soil onto the lower leaves

probable_causes.name: early blight
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: dark brown spots with concentric rings, like a target, on the older lower leaves, each with a yellow halo

organic.note: spray in the evening and cover the underside of the leaf

probable_causes.name: late blight
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: large grey-green water-soaked patches starting at the leaf margin, with a pale ring and sometimes white growth on the underside in damp weather

organic.note: mix fresh and use the same day

probable_causes.name: bacterial leaf spot
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: many small dark spots with a narrow yellow halo, which later dry and tear, giving the leaf a ragged look

organic.note: do not mix with a chemical fungicide in the same tank

probable_causes.name: powdery mildew
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: white powdery patches on the upper leaf surface that rub off between the fingers

probable_causes.name: sucking pest damage
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: yellow stipple mottling, curled leaves, sticky honeydew and sooty black mould, with small insects clustered on the leaf underside

organic.note: add a yellow sticky trap for every 10 plants

chemical.interval: one spray, repeat only after 15 days

probable_causes.name: leaf miner damage
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: pale winding trails inside the leaf, like a serpent line drawn under the surface

organic.note: pick and destroy the mined leaves first

chemical.interval: one spray, repeat only after 15 days

probable_causes.name: nutrient deficiency
probable_causes.distinguishing_symptom: even yellowing between green veins with no spots and no insects, usually on the older leaves first

chemical.dose: 5 g per litre of water as a foliar spray

organic_treatment.note: spray in the evening and wet both sides of the leaf

organic_treatment.interval: as a soil drench every 15 days
organic_treatment.note: use on the soil, not on the leaf

chemical_treatment.note: use only after confirming a fungal cause by the symptoms above
works on both bacterial spot and late blight

prevention: remove and burn the affected lower leaves, do not leave them in the field
switch from overhead watering to drip or basin watering so leaves stay dry
mulch the soil to stop rain splashing soil onto the lower leaves
stake the plants and keep 45 to 60 cm spacing so air moves freely
rotate to a non-host crop for two to three seasons
wash hands and tools after handling affected plants

urgency.trace: Damage is only just starting. Remove the affected leaves today and scout again in 3 days. A spray is usually not needed yet.
urgency.mild: Remove the affected leaves today, then spray the organic option within 2 days. Scout again after 7 days.
urgency.moderate: Act within 24 hours. Remove the affected leaves, spray, and check the neighbouring plants, because the damage is spreading.
urgency.severe: Act today. More than half the leaf is lost. Remove the badly affected leaves, spray, and ask your local agriculture extension officer to visit, because the whole plot is at risk.

scouting: check 10 plants in each corner of the field and 10 in the middle
look at the older lower leaves first, where most leaf disease starts
turn the leaves over and look for insects and their eggs on the underside
match what you see against the probable causes listed above before choosing a spray

region_notes.default: Spray only in calm weather and never within the pre-harvest interval shown for the product.
region_notes.tamil_nadu: During the north-east monsoon from October to December, long leaf wetness favours blight. Shorten the spray interval to 7 days and drain standing water from the field.
region_notes.punjab: Blight pressure rises in February and March. Avoid evening irrigation so leaves are dry overnight.
region_notes.maharashtra: In the kharif season, high humidity favours blight. Improve drainage and keep the field free of weeds.

sources: ICAR Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, integrated disease management advisories
Tamil Nadu Agricultural University Crop Protection Guide
Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee approved label claims

uncertain.headline_en: This image cannot be assessed reliably
uncertain.what_is_happening_en: Xaverix could not find a single clear leaf filling the frame, or the image sits outside the range this prototype was trained on. No verdict is given, because a wrong verdict would be worse than none.
prevention: hold the camera 20 to 30 cm from one leaf so the leaf fills most of the frame
photograph in daylight but not in direct glare, and avoid your own shadow
place the leaf against a plain background such as bare soil or a plain cloth
keep the camera steady and take the photo again if it looks blurred

urgency.trace: Retake the photograph following the guidance above.

urgency.severe: Retake the photograph following the guidance above.

scouting: if the leaf clearly looks damaged to your eye, trust your eye and ask your local agriculture extension officer
